title: Severe and Moderate Asthma Exacerbations in Asthmatic Children and Exposure to Ambient Air Pollutants.
ehr_evidence: We studied asthmatic children born between 1 April 1996 and 31 March 2011 in the province of Quebec (Canada) and identified from a population open birth cohort created with the Quebec Integrated Chronic Disease Surveillance System (QICDSS) [25].
summary: Population-based cohort study assessing the association between birth and time-dependent exposure to ambient air pollutants (NO2, O3, PM2.5) and severe asthma exacerbations in asthmatic children in Quebec, Canada.
key_findings: Of 162,752 asthmatic children followed, 35,229 had at least one exacerbation.
Time-dependent exposure to NO2 (IQR 4.95 ppb) was associated with an increased risk of exacerbation (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.058–1.131).
Time-dependent exposure to O3 (IQR 3.85 ppb) was associated with an increased risk of exacerbation (HR 1.052, 95% CI 1.037–1.066).
Time-dependent exposure to PM2.5 (IQR 1.82 µg/m3) was associated with an increased risk of exacerbation (HR 1.025, 95% CI 1.017–1.031).
Birth exposure to PM2.5 was positively associated with exacerbation risk (HR 1.051, 95% CI 1.049–1.053).
No significant associations were found between birth exposure to NO2 (HR 1.001, 95% CI 0.995–1.005) or O3 and exacerbations.
A significant effect modification was found between NO2 exposure and sex, with increased risk observed in girls.
population: Asthmatic children born 1996-2011 in Quebec, Canada (<13 years)
limitations: Health care service use definition may miss milder exacerbations
30-day buffer period may underestimate recurring events
Exposure assigned at postal code centroid causing measurement error
PM2.5 exposure constant over follow-up period
Lack of individual-level SES and secondhand smoke data
